life_summary: Henry Bennion Eyring was born on May 31, 1933, in Princeton, New Jersey, to a prominent family with connections to the LDS Church. Growing up in New Jersey provided him with exposure to the northeastern United States and a diverse cultural environment. Eyring received his education through university studies and developed interests in science, mathematics, and technology. He married Kathleen Johnson on July 27, 1962, at the LDS Church's Logan Temple, beginning a marriage that lasted 61 years until Kathleen's death on October 15, 2023. The couple built their life together while Eyring balanced scientific and professional pursuits with deep ecclesiastical commitments. Eyring's background in technology and analysis, combined with his spiritual conviction, made him a unique voice in modern church leadership.
church_summary: Henry B. Eyring served as a district missionary for the LDS Church while stationed at Sandia Base in New Mexico during his Air Force service, where he also worked analyzing weapons test data. He was later called to positions of increasing responsibility within church leadership, eventually being called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. Eyring has dedicated multiple temples including San Salvador El Salvador, Gilbert Arizona, Payson Utah, Indianapolis Indiana, and Philadelphia Pennsylvania. He also rededicated the Buenos Aires Argentina and Mexico City Mexico Temples. His published works emphasize faith, covenants, leadership, spiritual gifts, family, truth-seeking, and moral development. His teaching spans theological and practical dimensions, including works such as 'A Life Founded in Light and Truth' and 'Teaching Is a Moral Act.'
